Ethereum Foundation Sounds Alarm Over AI Threats

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (404 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a upcoming and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.
  • AI is identifying bugs in live software more promptly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.
  • As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a upcoming and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.

AI is identifying bugs in live software more promptly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.

As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.

For Ethereum developers, the immediate challenge is ensuring that bugs are not present in their software before an upgrade.

The longer-term challenge is mathematical. Ethereum uses digital signatures to identify who can spend funds and which validators have approved the state of the chain.

Wedderburn states that AI's advances in analyzing decades-old algorithms raise questions about the mathematical assumptions underlying those signatures that researchers should consider.

According to recent reports, it is not clear whether AI could break Ethereum's existing cryptography. However,  the Ethereum Foundation wants work on fresh cryptography to be underway.

After more than a year of considering various signature schemes, the Ethereum Foundation has decided to replace elliptic-curve signatures with hash-based cryptography.

The argument is that Ethereum already relies on cryptographic hash security, and by using hashes for signatures too, it can remove an additional assumption about the difficulty of solving mathematical problems associated with elliptic curves.

The proposal affects three areas of Ethereum.

It would see validators use hash-based keys for their signatures, which in turn changes how block finality is determined on the network.

Wallet developers would need to provide users with a way to transition their accounts to hash-based signatures.

And Ethereum's change to the cryptography used for commitments to data (blobs) that rollups publish to the network would require adjustments from rollups too.

According to recent reports, one challenge is the size of the signatures. Hash-based signatures are much larger, so developers need to consider how that affects the hardware needed to run a node at home.

According to recent reports, staking pools and multisig wallets would need adjustments too. So would smart contracts that rely on existing cryptography.

There will also be a need to adjust tools that rely on the signature scheme currently used by Ethereum validators (BLS).

Tech Report: Tesla stops selling every Cybertruck except the $109,990 Cyberbeast

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.
  • Sources indicate that the Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator reveals today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

Sources indicate that the Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator reveals today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.

A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

It has been revealed that on November 6, the same day Elon Musk declared the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

New inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search highlighted no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”.

Sources indicate that if there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

But the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”.

That’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Industry observers note that some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t said whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

This is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we said it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

If you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper fresh option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

In a recent development, XRP has printed a substantial exchange outflow, with 270 million XRP moving out of Uphold in 24 hours. That's three transfers of 90 million XRP each. The transfers raise more questions about what large holders are doing while XRP struggles below $1.

In a recent development, the three transfers went to rP2Sxx…jzmV, rhDoUm…LVNk and rKB4EP…YUs3. In total, 78 transfers crossed the 1 million XRP threshold, moving 523 million XRP. Of the transfers tracked, 31 worth a combined 75.8 million XRP were movements between wallets belonging to the same owners. Taking those out gives us a clearer picture of transfers to outside wallets.

More XRP was removed from known exchange wallets than added to them. Outflows reached 456.2 million XRP, while inflows sat at 181.7 million XRP. Uphold led with a net outflow of 269.1 million XRP. Robinhood saw the largest net inflow at 13.5 million XRP.

According to recent reports, inflows and outflows can reflect usual trading and investment activities, including investors moving funds into self-custody. It's crucial to keep in mind that if those tokens stay off exchanges, there could be less XRP readily available for sale. It's not clear whether there's any accumulation here. The next thing to watch is whether the funds stay in those wallets or move back to an exchange.

XRP was trading at $0.9376, up 1.15% over 24 hours. It traded as low as $0.9124 and as high as $1.024 in that window. XRP is still below all the major moving averages on the daily chart. The downtrend that took hold in November is still in place. RSI is borderline oversold, so selling pressure might be fading. A sustained recovery is yet to come.

Industry observers note that on November 22, the XRP Ledger recorded 2.8 million transactions and 3,833 new wallets. Payment volume reached 997.2 million XRP, while active accounts sat at 41,800. The network activity is still non-zero, though the transaction count is declining. The performance of XRP leaves a lot to be desired. The confirmation of a market recovery would only come if we witness stronger buying in the foreseeable future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Are Ripple’s XRP, Cardano (ADA), and Polygon (POL) losing their appeal among crypto investors in 2026? Ben Simpson, founder of crypto investment platform Collective Shift, has named all three among six altcoins he notes he wouldn’t touch with a 10-foot pole, citing concerns ranging from weak network activity and questionable valuations to intensifying competition. His blunt assessment raises fresh questions about which altcoins have the strongest fundamentals to survive the increasingly competitive crypto market.

In his post on X, Simpson acknowledged XRP’s role in enabling near-instant, inexpensive payments on the XRP Ledger but argued that the token lacks a compelling mechanism for capturing the value generated by Ripple’s business growth.

Recent findings suggest that XRP enables fast, low-cost payments on the XRP Ledger.My glitch with XRP is it's "value capture".When a business grows, I want to see how that success benefits the token I'm holding. In this case, there is none. Ripple can grow its revenue, but holders don't receive those….

Sources indicate that his main concern is that Ripple’s commercial success does not necessarily translate into direct financial benefits for XRP holders. Even as the San Francisco-headquartered company expands its revenue and boosts its payment operations, investors do not receive a share of those profits.

Sources indicate that he also pointed out that Ripple does not use its business earnings to buy back XRP, a mechanism that could potentially create additional demand for the token. For Simpson, the absence of both profit-sharing and a buyback program makes it difficult to establish a direct link between Ripple’s growing business and XRP’s price in the long term.

He considers these shortcomings significant enough to keep XRP off his investment list, despite the network’s payment capabilities.

Sources indicate that simpson also expressed reservations about Cardano, arguing that its adoption level does not justify its market valuation. Although ADA powers a blockchain designed to support smart contracts and decentralized applications, he believes the network is generating relatively little economic activity compared with its overall market size.

To support his argument, Simpson pointed to Cardano’s fee generation, claiming that the network collected just $140,000 in transaction fees over a 30-day period despite ADA carrying a market capitalization of approximately $7.5 billion.

For him, the disparity raises questions about whether Cardano is attracting enough consumers and developers to sustain its valuation. He believes a blockchain with such a substantial market capitalization should demonstrate considerably stronger usage and demand for its services.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Simpson’s concern is that Cardano needs to translate its technological ambitions and established ecosystem into greater real-world activity. Without a meaningful increase in network usage, he appears unconvinced that ADA offers an attractive investment proposition.

Polygon also made the list, with concerns centered on the growing competition in Ethereum’s scaling ecosystem. Although POL supports a network designed to make transactions faster and cheaper, the increasing number of competing blockchain solutions has made it harder for Polygon to maintain a distinctive advantage.

Simpson’s concern is that newer networks are offering similar benefits, including lower transaction costs and faster processing speeds, leaving Polygon with fewer obvious ways to differentiate itself.

With several projects competing for developers, consumers, and blockchain activity, POL faces the challenge of proving why it deserves a place ahead of its rivals.

Recent findings suggest that beyond XRP, Cardano, and Polygon, three other cryptocurrencies also fell short of Ben Simpson’s investment criteria: Sui (SUI), Ronin (RON), and Dogwifhat (WIF). Unlike his concerns about the first three crypto projects, his reservations about these tokens stem largely from changing investment convictions, disappointing adoption, and excessive reliance on market hype.

In a recent development, sui was among the projects Simpson previously held before changing his investment outlook. The high-speed blockchain is designed to support decentralized applications and transactions, but he eventually dumped his SUI holdings at a loss of between 20% and 30% after his investment thesis changed. He did not elaborate on the specific developments that prompted his decision.

Ronin was another project he abandoned after its growth failed to match his expectations. Initially attracted by the potential of blockchain gaming, the pundit bought into the network, which uses RON for transaction fees and staking. However, the anticipated expansion in gaming adoption did not materialize as he had hoped, prompting him to exit the position relatively quickly. He argued that strong sector potential means little without meaningful retail participation.

It has been revealed that WIF, meanwhile, represented a different kind of investment mistake. Simpson admitted that his decision to buy the Solana-based meme coin was driven largely by hype rather than underlying fundamentals. After his investment thesis changed, he sold his holdings to limit further losses.

His experience with WIF appears to have reinforced his preference for cryptocurrencies backed by stronger fundamentals rather than speculative excitement.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) community members have released a new block explorer for Shibarium, the layer-2 network of the SHIB ecosystem, and Shiba Inu lead Shytoshi Kusama has remained silent on X since May.

Recent findings suggest that shiba Inu community veteran Mazrael announced the new explorer, scan.shibfun.app, in an X post. "Shibarium has a new block explorer," he wrote. According to Mazrael, the explorer was "built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look.".

The launch comes as SHIB trades near its lowest levels in years. In November, the price of SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021, and on Nov. 22, the token traded at around $0.00000362, according to CoinMarketCap.

Recent findings suggest that according to the post, owners can type a .shib name in the search bar and land on the wallet linked to it, and the explorer also demonstrates new Shiboshis from Shibarium every day. For developers, Mazrael listed contract verification, read and write functions for contracts, the activity of ERC-4337 smart wallets, and a free API, which he described as "Etherscan-style too." Method names are decoded as well, and in Mazrael's words, there are "no more mystery 0x codes." The explorer also has a DApps page with Shibarium games and apps, and a button that adds Shibarium to a wallet in one click.

In a recent development, the work on the explorer is not finished yet. "Live blocks are complete now, and older history indexing," Mazrael wrote. On Tuesday, the explorer itself highlighted that 3% of Shibarium blocks had been indexed, and a notice on the site noted that some of the counts may be inaccurate. Mazrael added that the new explorer can be found on Shib.io under ShibWatch.

Recent findings suggest that shytoshi Kusama's last post or interaction on X dates back to May 13, 2026. In September, Kusama changed his X bio to "Polish" and his location to "Close," and he has not explained the meaning of either word. The official Shibarium account on X has not posted since July 13, 2026.

Still, Shibarium updates kept coming from community members. In October, Mazrael mentioned that CreateX, a standard factory for deploying contracts at the same address on different chains, went live on Shibarium. According to Mazrael, all 12 Safe v1.4.1 contracts were deployed to their canonical addresses through the Safe Singleton Factory, and x402 went live too, so AI agents can now pay in SHIB, TREAT and wrapped BONE.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

According to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

Home » Crypto Market News » Why Bitcoin Fell Below $60K Despite Nvidia’s 31% Surge.

While tech stocks celebrated Jensen Huang’s return, on-chain metrics suggest crypto traders face a very different test.

Bitcoin (BTC) briefly fell to $59,400 after failing to sustain a rally triggered by Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO —largely because the bounce was fueled by short-lived enthusiasm rather than genuine spot demand or improved crypto fundamentals.

While Nvidia (NVDA) shares surged more than 30% and major U.S. stock indexes recorded one of their best sessions in years on Monday, November 23, Bitcoin’s price reversed its initial recovery within about 12 hours, raising questions about buying demand across the cryptocurrency market.

In a recent development, bitcoin climbed toward an intraday high of $64,500 following Nvidia’s announcement before retreating below $60,000. The reversal contrasted with Nvidia’s 31% gain, the Nasdaq’s 6.51% advance and the S&P 500’s 4.73% increase.

According to Santiment’s latest market intelligence report, Bitcoin’s initial recovery was driven mainly by a wave of optimism and FOMO across financial markets, rather than any real improvement in demand for BTC.

Santiment’s Trending Words Dashboard recorded a sharp increase in mentions of Nvidia and Jensen Huang across cryptocurrency discussions on November 23, producing the largest single-day spike over the past month.

According to recent reports, “Huang’s return provided an immediate reason for investors to become more confident in Nvidia and its surrounding AI ecosystem,” the Santiment report states. “However, nothing about the announcement directly improved Bitcoin’s adoption, increased demand for BTC, or resolved the selling pressure that had dominated cryptocurrency markets for weeks.”.

In a recent development, still, the report noted that AI and significant data altcoins could hold long-term potential. For Bitcoin, however, rather than confirming a new bullish trend, the rally became another example of how FOMO can punish traders who mistake a temporary market reaction for a lasting shift in fundamentals.

Despite the underwhelming price action, Santiment’s on-chain data highlighted an unexpected divergence.

Around November 20, the analytics firm recorded roughly 750,400 daily active addresses and 332,820 newly introduced addresses, pointing to a notable rise in network participation even as prices weakened.

Daily active addresses measure how many unique blockchain addresses participate in transactions, while network growth tracks newly created active addresses.

Both metrics climbed during the downturn, indicating that underlying blockchain usage remained resilient despite falling market value.

Santiment cautioned that the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday may introduce another layer of uncertainty. Trading activity typically thins out during holiday-shortened weeks, allowing smaller groups of buyers and sellers to trigger outsized price swings amid lower liquidity.

Markets are also looking ahead to Wednesday’s October PCE inflation report and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book, both of which could shift rate expectations ahead of the Fed’s December 8–9 policy meeting.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin traders are watching for a potential retest of the $56,000 level, which could mark a local market bottom.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer remarked in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer announced earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

According to recent reports, production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the new i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen noted in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The tech giant also remarked investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW mentioned several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

However, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

Industry observers note that while development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council stated the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.

#87280. How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2193 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

How Sculpt Became the Fitness Space’s Buzziest—and Vaguest—Workout

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay.
  • Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture.
  • Sources indicate that now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By definition, the term sculpt means making something by carving stone or molding clay. It’s an art form, a manipulation of material to achieve a desired end result that’s aesthetically appealing.

Over the years, however, the term has also become ubiquitous in fitness culture. We talk about sculpting one's back or legs, implying some kind of crafting of muscles, as if treating the human form like a sculpture. In fact, check the group class schedule of any gym these days, and you’ll likely spot the term “sculpt” appear somewhere on the lineup—directing toward some variation of a Pilates mat or strength training class, often involving lower weights and higher reps.

Sources indicate that now, the term is prolific in fitness classes and social media alike, that the meaning is a bit murky—which begs the question, what does “sculpt” really mean in the context of exercise? Is it a legitimate term or nothing more than strategic marketing language?

Recent findings suggest that the exercise term actually dates back decades, with the first mentions appearing in fitness publications in the late 1970s. “It comes out of bodybuilding culture, which became more prominent in that period […] and you started to see the term ‘body sculpture,’” says Natalia Mehlman Petrezela, PhD, a historian and author of Fit Nation: The Gains and Pains of America’s Exercise Obsession. And while there’s no clear record of who coined the term in a fitness context, there is speculation that it may have been inspired by German strongman Eugen Sandow (often called the "father of modern bodybuilding"), who referenced Greco-Roman sculptures as examples of the “ideal” physique in the late 19th century.

According to recent reports, in the 1980s, the idea of sculpting your muscles started to become much more mainstream, with the rise of aerobics, toning workouts, and fitness videos, states physical therapist and trainer Shannon Ritchey, PT, DPT, founder of Evlo Fitness. As instructors began using the term to describe and market workouts designed to shape and define specific muscles, “sculpting” became part of the everyday fitness vocabulary.

The term also taps into something more personal: this idea that we have the power to change the shape of our own physiques. “I think that it really gained momentum because one, it kind of speaks to the artistry of the body or the artistry of fitness. Also, there's so much individual agency in this,” claims Petrezela. “It isn't about you just having the right genetics. Instead, you as an artist have the power to sculpt your own body.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the 1990s, however, the revered muscular look brought about by ’80s fitness culture made way for a celebration of thinner, more waifish bodies. “There was—and this is still the case—a lot of fear around getting too bulky,” says Petrezela. The term sculpting, however, molded into a promise of strength training without gaining too much muscle, which felt more palatable to women who feared such a physique.

“What's interesting is that we've changed the language over the years, but we're still selling women a very similar idea: that certain exercises will create a long, lean, toned appearance, while others will make them bulky,” indicates Ritchey.

Industry observers note that if you worked out in the 2010s, you probably remember “sculpt” becoming a fixture of the boutique fitness boom. Still, while studio culture has waxed and waned over the last 20 years, the term has only gained traction, popping up across social media and on class schedules everywhere (think Pilates sculpt, yoga sculpt, and seemingly endless variations), notes Laura Girard, CPT, a NASM personal trainer and co-host of the Fit Literate podcast.

Sources indicate that girard speculates that the popularity of sculpt classes may be buoyed by the widespread craving for more community in a post-pandemic world. After all, group fitness can be a fantastic third space. But there's another reason “sculpt” makes for such an appealing class name: It signals a particular kind of workout experience. Girard has observed “sculpt” used “almost like a dog whistle that [suggests] this class is going to be friendly for women and not scary, but still intense,” she says.

There's an aesthetic appeal, too. Petrezela believes the term’s resurgence of sorts has to do with how weightlifting and building muscle are very much having a moment, yet longstanding fears around getting “bulky” haven’t entirely disappeared. “It doesn't hurt that we are in a very, very image-driven moment in fitness culture,” she states. “We're not just looking at the images in magazines that come out once a month, but our [social media] feeds are nonstop bodies all day—many of which are shared by influencers who have their own plans for how you can sculpt a body that looks just like theirs, or so they say.”.

According to recent reports, if you were to ask 10 different people on the street what a “sculpt class” is, you may get 10 different answers. To some, sculpt is synonymous with a mat Pilates routine, to others it might be a strength-training session, and to others it might be a yoga practice involving light dumbbells. So, can all of these workouts really fall under the same umbrella? And when a class promises to “sculpt,” is that an actual measurable result your muscles can deliver—or a feeling the name is designed to sell?

According to the experts, it’s largely the latter. “In a world where two things are popular—strength training and being very thin—’sculpting’ seems to be an appealing middle ground from a marketing perspective,” notes Ritchey. “It promises ‘long, lean muscle tone’ without the perceived risk of building too much muscle.”.

She adds that “sculpt” is often used interchangeably with “toning,” which she describes as a “made-up term” that typically refers to changing your body composition (a.k.a., reducing fat and building muscle).

Because there's no single definition, what you actually do in a sculpt class can vary considerably. Still, Girard notes many sculpt classes share certain characteristics: lighter weights, choreography-inspired movements, and a lot of mat work. She also notes that while exercises are often fatiguing (think: that familiar muscle-burning sensation), they’re not necessarily pushing you to muscle failure via progressive overload (which is necessary for hypertrophy, or muscle-building).

In a recent development, ritchey, who taught a sculpt class years ago, recalls using dumbbells and bodyweight for high reps. “We would do an entire three- to four-minute song of squats and lunges. That’s likely over 100 squats in a row, which burns and feels hard,” she says. Of course, it’s certainly possible to promote muscle-building with a low-weight, high-rep range, granted the programming is intentional. “But we know that if you could physically do more than about 30 reps in a row, the load is too light to build muscle.”.

According to recent reports, it’s important to note that a workout doesn't have to maximize muscle growth to be worthwhile. Certain sculpt classes can offer other benefits, from muscular endurance to simply providing motivation and enjoyment of exercising, often in a group setting. But if your primary goal is to significantly increase muscle size or change your body composition, not every sculpt class will provide the progressive resistance training needed to make that happen.

That’s where experts say the “sculpt” terminology can get confusing or misleading for some people. Girard fears that the language surrounding sculpt workouts reinforces misconceptions about women's bodies and what exercise can realistically change. “Sculpt as a verb is not a thing we can do to our bodies,” she notes. “We can gain or lose muscle. We can gain or lose fat, but that's more the role of nutrition. But we can't control how those muscles look.”.

Sources indicate that in other words, there's no special exercise technique that creates “long, lean” muscles instead of so-called “bulky” ones. Your genetics influence your muscle shape, while your training can affect how much muscle you build. And the workout's name doesn't change those underlying principles.

What’s more, at a time when there’s seemingly no consensus on how to talk about bodies or fitness in an empowering, nonoffensive way, Girard sees the term “sculpt” as potential coded language. While we may have mostly done away with, say, “bikini body shred” language in 2026, she fears that this nebulous term may be subliminally hinting at the same idea.

And while there's absolutely “nothing wrong with having aesthetic goals,” Ritchey stresses, “women deserve accurate information about how to achieve them.” If body recomp is their goal, they would have more success lifting close to failure and focusing on diet.”.

Ultimately, your muscles don’t know whether you’re in a sculpt class or a traditional strength workout. Instead, they respond to the resistance, effort, and progression involved.

It has been revealed that “It’s funny because while all these trends come and go—and we will see sculpt come and go, too—the science never changes,” Ritchey says. “People just aren’t patient enough with the basics, so they jump on the latest trend thinking it will finally be the golden ticket to seeing results.”.

Because “sculpt” has no one definition, the quality, intensity, and overall experience of classes bearing the name can vary widely, too.

According to recent reports, beyond the workout itself, Girard points out that some sculpt classes can come with an unspoken expectation about who belongs in the room. As she’s observed: “These classes tend to be a self-selecting in-group. You may only see one type of body, or one specific outfit [...] That doesn’t mean it’s wrong or bad to be in a different outfit or in a different body, but it sure can feel that way.”.

Sources indicate that of course, there are also plenty of classes with “sculpt” in the name that are fantastic, inclusive workouts. This all boils down to the instructor, methods, and specific exercises they choose to incorporate—along with the type of community they cultivate. And, in many cases—particularly with larger studios or gyms—instructors have no say in what their class is actually called. “A lot of times, they're just doing what's trending to get people in the door,” indicates Girard.

So if you’ve been curious to try a new sculpt class at a local studio—by all means, go for it. Just be sure to go into it with eyes wide open, and give yourself permission to stop or pause or walk away if it doesn’t feel like a productive or positive environment for you. Pay attention to how the workout feels, how the instructor coaches, and whether the environment makes you feel welcome. One potential red flag? Aggressive “bikini body” messaging or marketing that frames building muscle as something to avoid. As Girard emphasizes, “It is definitely, definitely is not.”.

As the experts agree: Finding a form of movement you enjoy is the most key ingredient for establishing a healthy, consistent fitness routine. “My advice would be to ask yourself why you're doing these classes. Is it because you genuinely enjoy them? Or is it because you believe the burning sensation means you're toning and sculpting your muscles? Because those are two very different things,” indicates Ritchey.

Recent findings suggest that have a sculpt workout you absolutely love? That’s wonderful, too. Finding movement you genuinely enjoy is one of the best ways to build a fitness routine you'll actually stick with. The important thing is understanding what you're getting out of it—and whether that aligns with what you're hoping to achieve.

“I want women to feel empowered to choose exercise based on what they enjoy and what actually works,” says Ritchey.

For someone primarily focused on building muscle, Ritchey recommends treating sculpt classes as opportunities for cardio or simply enjoyable movement, rather than as a replacement for progressive strength training.

They can even be great options for off days from lifting. “I don’t want to discourage anyone from moving,” she says. “But at the same time, we deserve to understand what is marketing and what our bodies actually respond to. We are all busy and tired and stressed [and] I want women to know how to best use their efforts to match their goals.”.

Recent findings suggest that appreciate the workout for what it is, understand what it isn't, and choose what works for you. That, in fact, is the true artistry of exercise.

Growing stablecoin supply and actually using that supply are two different things.

Interestingly, this difference is becoming important in comparing Ethereum [ETH] and XRPL’s on-chain activity around RLUSD. On-chain data highlights that nearly $11.716 billion worth of RLUSD was transacted on the XRP Ledger and Ethereum in the week up to the 1st of November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the key takeaway? XRPL handled the larger share of RLUSD activity. As the chart below shows, $6.699 billion was transacted on the XRPL network, representing 57% of the total RLUSD volume. The Ethereum blockchain had total transactions of $5.017 billion (42.82%).

So, although there is more RLUSD on the Ethereum blockchain, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume.

Notably, RLUSD’s DEX activity on XRPL is also picking up.

It has been revealed that the total DEX volume reached an all-time high of $596.2 million in the week ending August. While volume has dropped in recent weeks, it has been consistently above $70 million per week for the last 10 weeks.

It has been revealed that more recently, volume has picked up again, exceeding $200 million per week. This is significantly higher than previous averages of approximately $15 million.

So, while there is more RLUSD on Ethereum, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume and growing DEX activity. This suggests that more RLUSD is being used on XRPL, making it a network to watch as the stablecoin continues to grow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Flop Labs has declared a minor delay to the launch of its public testnet, pushing back from its previous goal of 15:00 (UTC+8) on November 24.

It's unclear what the reason for the delay is, although the team does expect to launch the testnet before 18:00 (UTC+8) the same day.

Possible reasons for the delay could include conducting final checks, calibrating nodes, validator onboarding, load testing, etc. (although Flop Labs has not confirmed any of these to be the reason for the delay).

It does not appear that Flop Labs has any prepares to move the testnet launch to another day.

Flop Labs is building FLOP Network, a blockchain serving as a settlement layer for what it calls the "agentic economy". This would enable AI agents to make payments for computation (e.g. model inference) and memory services, and provide rewards to GPU miners that contribute their computational power to fulfill these requests.

Computation is verified via Flop Labs' "Proof of Useful Inference", which entails miners providing evidence that they've carried out the desired AI computation, and validators checking this evidence.

It has been revealed that why does this matter? FLOP Network would enable agents to make payments for computation, memory, etc. Flop Labs' main competitors include Akash Network and io.net (both of which facilitate access to compute/gpu resources in a decentralized manner), as well as Render Network (which started out facilitating decentralized graphics rendering but has since expanded into AI/compute more broadly).

While Flop Labs' competitors also facilitate access to compute, Flop Labs' main differentiating factor appears to be its focus on facilitating agent-to-agent commerce and computation-verification.

It has been revealed that flop Labs is led by Arthur Hayes, co-founder of crypto exchange BitMEX and current chief investment officer at Maelstrom. The rest of Flop Labs' team includes Sergey Vidyuk (ex-Deutsche Bank/BitMEX) as CTO, and Shu Duan (with experience in investment banking and crypto asset management) as chief strategy officer.

The testnet would be an opportunity to see if Flop Labs can successfully build out its envisioned agentic economy.

  • The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.
  • We knew it was coming soon after the new model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the new model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD declared on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.

Like many of its new flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division stated third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it rolled out in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

Sources indicate that the Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

Will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

Crypto wallet provider Trezor has issued a security warning to cryptocurrency customers following a recent theft report: "Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.".

Recent findings suggest that according to Onchain Lens, a user reported losing over $600,000 across TRON and Solana while using an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1. Both the Trezor Safe 7 and the Exodus wallet were reportedly affected. The victim had been using a Trezor Safe 7 for nearly two months.

According to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

In a recent development, the device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

It has been revealed that the user said $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Sources indicate that another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Industry observers note that trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

On November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is currently no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

According to recent reports, trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are currently no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

@OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official ENHANCEMENT: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further update, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the manufacturer and indicated no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

This appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an vital security warning: people should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

In a recent development, the new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.

It has been revealed that volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.

The VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.

Volkswagen mentioned it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).

The production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine latest models VW intends to launch by 2027.

Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.

The VW Group’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.

All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen stated the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.

In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

According to recent reports, this PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or issues with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

There are two main proposed changes:.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

According to recent reports, this PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

Sources indicate that this is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's vital not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

It has been revealed that for everyday consumers, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, submitted by developer Jean Pablo on Nov.
  • The proposal could particularly benefit wallets such as Electrum, which supports Bitcoin's Lightning Network and relies on external servers for some blockchain information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin developers have proposed a new verification system that would allow lightweight wallets to independently authenticate transaction signatures recorded on the blockchain.

According to recent reports, the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, submitted by developer Jean Pablo on Nov. 22, addresses a limitation in how wallets verify transaction information received from external servers.

The proposal could particularly benefit wallets such as Electrum, which supports Bitcoin's Lightning Network and relies on external servers for some blockchain information.

At the moment, lightweight wallets can verify that a transaction was included in a Bitcoin block using a cryptographic proof tied to its transaction ID, or txid.

However, that identifier excludes witness data, which contains signatures and other information used to authorize spending under Bitcoin's Segregated Witness (SegWit) system.

Consequently, a wallet could successfully verify a transaction's inclusion while holding witness data that differs from what miners actually included in the block.

Pablo's proposal addresses this discrepancy by introducing standardized witness transaction inclusion proofs built around a second identifier, known as the witness transaction ID, or wtxid.

Unlike the conventional transaction ID, the wtxid incorporates witness data, allowing wallets to verify that the full transaction they received matches the version included in a mined block.

The proposed system connects that identifier to Bitcoin's existing witness commitment, which is recorded in the block's coinbase transaction. A second cryptographic proof then connects the coinbase transaction to the block header.

An ordinary proof checks the transaction ID. The draft adds a path from the witness data to the same block header.

A wallet can compare the witness data it received with what a valid block committed to.

It has been revealed that the proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

The diagram follows the two proof paths described in the draft and the wallet verification flow in the Bitcoin Core discussion.

The proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

Together, these checks allow wallets to authenticate witness data without downloading and examining the entire block.

The development follows an earlier request from Electrum contributor SomberNight, who sought witness inclusion proofs to strengthen transaction verification for the wallet's Lightning Network functionality.

Lightning wallets interact with Bitcoin's underlying blockchain when opening, closing and monitoring payment channels, making reliable transaction information particularly important.

The proposed verification system would allow such wallets to independently confirm the witness data supplied by servers while continuing to operate without storing complete blockchain data.

The request previously prompted work on Bitcoin Core, where developers explored extending existing transaction proof commands to cover witness information.

That pull request closed in May without being merged, and developer Sjors Provoost later continued the effort through a separate implementation that introduced commands to generate and verify witness proofs.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin Knots introduced experimental witness-proof support in version 29.1, and Electrum developers have been working on related protocol changes.

However, these efforts use different proof formats, creating compatibility challenges between wallets and the servers providing blockchain information.

Pablo's proposal attempts to resolve those differences by specifying two binary formats and a JSON representation for exchanging and verifying proofs.

The first format provides a separate cryptographic proof for each transaction, while the second reduces duplicated information when verifying multiple transactions together.

In one example involving 10 transactions, the second format reduced proof data from 4,523 bytes to 3,325 bytes, approximately a 26% reduction.

The proposal also includes a Python reference implementation and 93 test cases designed to establish consistent verification behavior across software implementations.

Of those tests, 31 cover proofs that should be accepted, while 62 cover invalid proofs that verification software must reject.

The specification would give Bitcoin Core, Electrum and other wallet developers a common framework for implementing witness verification.

Pablo has requested feedback on the proposed formats and verification requirements, leaving developers to determine whether a shared standard can replace the experimental approaches already in use.

Oluwapelumi values Bitcoin's potential. He imparts insights on a range of topics like DeFi, hacks, mining and culture, underlining transformative power.

It has been revealed that the side pockets are small, but hold small essentials like a credit card, key, or energy gels for long runs. Rinnai’s newly introduced heat pump water heaters get smarter – and easier to install

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rinnai has introduced a new lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.
  • The REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes.
  • Industry observers note that heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rinnai has introduced a new lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.

The REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.

Industry observers note that heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.

In a recent development, rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.

The lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.

It has been revealed that there are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.

Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.

An optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.

Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.

Wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.

The units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai says the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.

Sources indicate that the series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.

I’m very happy with my hybrid heat pump water heater. I run it in heat pump only mode in summer and it helps cool the house for free. For anyone on the fence, especially your utility offers a rebate, it’s definitely worth looking at.

Rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday morning, the crypto market gave back almost all of the gains it made after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO on Monday. According to CoinMarketCap data, the price of Bitcoin stood at around $60,000 on Tuesday morning, and on Monday evening, Bitcoin was trading as high as $64,372. XRP was back at $0.93 on Tuesday morning after the cryptocurrency reached $1.026 on Monday.

Industry observers note that the price of Ethereum was between $1,680 and $1,695 on Tuesday morning, according to CoinMarketCap. In addition, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index stood at 10 on Tuesday, and the index showed extreme fear in the market.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had $569.7 million in net outflows on Monday, Nov. 23, SoSoValue data reveals. Spot XRP ETFs in the U.S. also saw outflows on Monday, and the total amount of these outflows was $2.5 million.

On Monday, Nvidia's board voted to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO after input from senior levels of the U.S. government, according to the company's press release. Nvidia shares closed 31.5% higher at $165.05, and the company added $954.3 billion in market value in one session. That is more than twice the previous one-day record of $450 billion that Microsoft set in July.

The S&P 500 gained 4.73% on Monday, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.86%. Bitcoin followed the rally and rose to $64,372 on Monday evening, and XRP reached $1.026.

Nvidia shares were down 4.1% at $158.03 in premarket trading on Tuesday, and Nasdaq 100 futures lost 1.62% on Tuesday morning. The VIX rose 8.72% to 28.93 at the same time.

Anthropic shares traded below the $83 IPO price on Tuesday. Earlier, all seven co-founders of the AI tech giant filed to sell a combined $1.96 billion worth of Anthropic stock, or about $280 million each, and there was also news about internal safety problems at Anthropic.

According to CoinGlass data, 146,356 traders were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and the total amount of liquidations reached $875 million.

Short sellers were hit first during Monday's rally, and short positions accounted for $473 million of the total. The largest single liquidation was a $17.83 million BTC-USD position on Hyperliquid. On Tuesday morning, it was the turn of long positions. Over the past 12 hours, longs accounted for $168.85 million out of $207.37 million in liquidations.

Sources indicate that bitcoin dropped as low as $59,366 and was trading at around $60,300 on Tuesday morning, down 1.5% over 24 hours. Bitcoin liquidations amounted to $372.68 million. In addition, open interest in Bitcoin futures rose 1.31% to $39.49 billion as the price was going down.

XRP followed Bitcoin and fell from $1.026 to $0.9238 before it stabilized at around $0.93. XRP liquidations reached $14.05 million over 24 hours, and 3,350 traders were affected. The Coinbase premium for XRP was -0.13%, and the premium for XRP in South Korea was 1.56%.

It has been revealed that bitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes also commented on the Nvidia rally. According to Hayes, Nvidia's rise is the worst-case scenario for crypto portfolios. Hayes stated that crypto needs a crash in U.S. stocks that would force the Fed to start printing money again.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a forfeiture complaint against more than $1.1 billion in USDC stablecoins. The funds were stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers on Oct. 29, and Circle helped the authorities with the case. According to the Department of Justice, North Korean hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in the attack. Earlier in November, the department noted that U.S. authorities and private companies had frozen more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds.

According to recent reports, the Ethereum Foundation also addressed the threat of artificial intelligence. According to the foundation, AI is a more urgent threat to the network than quantum computers. In a blog post, the EF developers stated that AI finds vulnerabilities in code faster than auditors can check them, and they also said that AI could break mathematical algorithms that have been used for decades.

EF researcher Justin Drake also spoke about Ethereum's move to hash-based cryptography at Devcon 8 in Mumbai. Drake mentioned that he hoped to complete the transition by December 2028. Earlier, the Ethereum Foundation set December 2029 as the deadline for quantum resistance in its roadmap.

There was other news from regulators and banks as well:.

According to Grayscale, the current bear market for Bitcoin has lasted 411 days, and it is the longest one in history. Still, Grayscale called it the mildest one. Bitcoin fell 56% from its October 2025 peak of $124,824 to last week's low of $55,254, according to Grayscale.

Galaxy Research put the drawdown at 53%. According to Galaxy, Bitcoin lost 85%, 84% and 77% in the bear markets of 2013–2015, 2017–2018 and 2021–2022, respectively.

The market capitalization of altcoins excluding Bitcoin and Ethereum dropped to $630.71 billion on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that according to CoinGlass data, large buy orders for Bitcoin on OKX and Binance were placed between $59,137 and $59,366 on Tuesday, and $30.3 million worth of long positions could be liquidated in the same range. A large sell order for Bitcoin was placed on Hyperliquid at $60,682, and $64.4 million worth of short positions could be liquidated near $63,996.

The max pain price for Bitcoin options expiring on Nov. 25 stood at $61,000, and the notional value of these options was $642.3 million.

For XRP, liquidations data shows a buy order on Gate at $0.9240 and $577,200 worth of long positions that could be liquidated at $0.9187. Sell orders for XRP on Gate and Hyperliquid were placed between $0.9340 and $0.9444, and $1.4 million worth of short positions could be liquidated at $0.9887.

U.S. junk-bond yields rose to 8.46% at the Nov. 20 close as investment-grade yields fell, according to ICE BofA data published Nov. 23 by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Bond investors demanded a bigger premium to own the weakest corporate debt. That gives Bitcoin buyers a separate gauge of risk appetite after Monday's rebound lost momentum.

It has been revealed that the yield on the U.S. high-yield index rose from 8.25% on Nov. 16 to 8.46% on Nov. 20. The biggest yield move among the three corporate indexes was in bonds rated CCC or lower. Its effective yield rose from 17.88% to 18.61%.

Industry observers note that over the same dates, the investment-grade corporate yield fell from 5.95% to 5.84%. The two-year Treasury yield fell from 4.83% to 4.63%.

Industry observers note that the gap over the Treasury curve widened across all three ICE BofA corporate bond indexes between Nov. 16 and Nov. 20, 2026.

The option-adjusted spread for bonds rated CCC and lower widened 92 basis points, compared with 42 for high yield overall and 8 for investment grade.

It has been revealed that CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index. Option-adjusted spreads measure the yield premium over the Treasury curve after accounting for embedded options.

ICE BofA daily closing option-adjusted spreads via FRED. Change equals the Nov. 20 close minus the Nov. 16 close. One percentage point equals 100 basis points. Bars share a 0–100 basis point scale.

In a recent development, CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index. Option-adjusted spreads measure the yield premium over the Treasury curve after accounting for embedded options.

Effective yields reflect the returns implied by the prices and payments of bonds in each index. The terms of any new financing would depend on the issuer and the deal. An option-adjusted spread measures the extra yield over the Treasury curve after accounting for options built into the bonds.

Industry observers note that the high-yield spread widened from 3.34 to 3.76 percentage points between Nov. 16 and Nov. 20. The CCC-and-lower spread rose from 13.10 to 14.02 points. The investment-grade spread widened from 0.90 to 0.98 points. Even as investment-grade yields fell, investors demanded a bigger premium to hold those bonds over Treasuries.

Daily closing effective yields for ICE BofA U.S. corporate bond indexes. CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index.

Source: ICE BofA / FRED · Investment grade · ICE BofA / FRED · High yield · ICE BofA / FRED · CCC and lower.

According to recent reports, the authors of The Crypto Cycle and US Monetary Policy, a 2023 IMF working paper, found that U.S. monetary tightening weighed on a common factor in crypto prices through investors' willingness to take risk, a channel they also identified in equities. The latest bond and ETF readings are consistent with shared caution, though they cannot explain Monday's Bitcoin price moves on their own.

In a recent development, further widening in high-yield spreads alongside continued spot Bitcoin ETF outflows would point to caution persisting in both markets. Narrower spreads alongside renewed ETF inflows would support the case for a broader recovery in risk appetite. Sustained ETF inflows while spreads stay wide would suggest demand through those funds can recover even as bond investors remain wary.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Monday New York trading session open brought a flurry of volatility to Bitcoin [BTC] and the rest of the market. Nvidia’s stock soared 31% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately.

Combined with the oversold market conditions, the tech and AI-sector stock market bounce helped Bitcoin rally to a local high of $64,603.

Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, BTC was back below the $61,000 mark. Its rally liquidated $520.89 million in short positions across the crypto market, including $225.58 million for Bitcoin alone.

The BTC spot ETF flows on Monday measured -$60.4 million, extending the bearish market sentiment and highlighting the lack of demand.

According to recent reports, the MVRV Z-score measures the difference between market capitalization and realized capitalization. It displayed a reading of 0.24 and has fallen by 0.11 over the past week, reaching among the lowest in four years.

Recent findings suggest that it has remained positive for 1,410 days, reported crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. A drop below zero would mean that the market cap has fallen below realized cap, a sign of deep capitulation.

Another metric that reached some of its lowest levels in four years was the supply in profit. It compares the market price with the last moved price of coins in the circulating supply.

Less than half of the coins are in profit, mirroring the lows from the previous bear market lows of late 2022.

It has been revealed that in August, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on Binance peaked at +2.41b. This peak showed heavy market buying as prices climbed toward $80k. Yet, as the price pushed to the local high at $87k, the CVD on Binance declined to -6b.

This was a bearish divergence; rising sell market orders captured take-profit behavior, while late entrants and leverage hunts pushed prices higher.

In November, across all exchanges, the CVD’s decline accelerated alongside price drawdown, and Binance’s CVD figure reached -21b, wrote crypto analyst FundingVest.

Price and CVD were aligned bearishly.

If the falling CVD momentum slows down while Bitcoin’s price continues its descent, it could be a constructive sign that will considerably increase the chances of a recovery.

Tesla Cybercab orders open at $29,990 + $299/mo, only in Robotaxi zones

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek
